Software Engineer \| Fullstack
 

  





**Location:** 

 Hybrid — Washington, DC
 




  





 Who We Are
 


 LoVasco helps organizations deliver exceptional benefits and retirement programs to the people they employ, while also stewarding the financial well\-being of individuals in and out of the workplace. We engage clients who genuinely prioritize their employees, and we give them the tools, education, and programs that help their people achieve financial security for themselves and their families. That's our "why," and it's what motivates us.
 




  





 What We're Building, and Why
 


 Engineering at LoVasco was born out of a simple desire: to solve our own problems. A business like ours can string together a dozen flexible, off\-the\-shelf tools to deliver its services—and for a long time, that's exactly what we did. A stack of subscriptions, a web of workarounds, software that "does everything" but nothing quite the way we want it.
 





 We believe in purpose\-built software. Opinionated design. Polished, thoughtful workflows that bring clarity to our teams, elevate what we're capable of, are a joy to use, and are genuinely powerful. At the end of the day, our goal is to deliver the best possible experience to our clients—and we believe that owning the software we use to deliver our services, and that our clients and their participants use to interact with us, is the best way to do it.
 





 What we're building is platform that serves as an “operating system” for our consulting business. For our teams, it's where we manage and make sense of our data, sharpen the insights we deliver, and automate the "work around work" so our people can focus on how best to serve our clients. For our clients, it's a centralized place to engage with those insights, own their data, and measure the impact of their programs. For participants, it's an education experience and a set of tools that feel tailored to them, are genuinely useful, and help them get the most out of their benefits.
 




  





 Our Tech Stack
 


 We build with React and Next.js on the frontend, NestJS for our API, Prisma as our ORM, and PostgreSQL for our database, all hosted on AWS. We manage nearly all of our infrastructure with Terraform, and DevOps and CI/CD are first\-class parts of how we work.
 





 Experience with this exact stack is welcome, but it isn't a requirement. A strong foundation in modern web frameworks and databases, and the discipline to ship and operate software well, matters far more than any single tool—we can teach the specifics. What we're looking for is genuine technical competence and an people who love their craft.
 




  





 Your Role
 


 We're looking for fullstack engineers. You'll work across the entire stack, designing, building, and maintaining features end\-to\-end—from the database to the interface—and help own the infrastructure and deployment pipelines that keep our platform reliable.
 





 Because projects here begin with open questions rather than finished specifications, you'll help shape what we build: translating user feedback into the right work, scoping projects, writing RFCs, documenting decisions, and taking part in our planning cycles.
 





 The five key responsibilities for this role are:
 





 \-     
 
**Migrating a core consulting team onto our platform:** 

 modeling their data, rebuilding the workflows they rely on off their patchwork of legacy SaaS tools.
 





 \-     
 
**Building the CRM\-style interfaces our teams live in every day:** 

 the data entry, organization, and record\-keeping tools that keep client information accurate and usable.
 





 \-     
 
**Turning dense benefits and retirement data into clear, comparative reporting:** 

 client\- and participant\-facing views that make complex programs easy to understand and act on.
 





 \-     
 
**Contributing to our REST API:** 

 implementing business logic that is well\-tested, performant, and built to last.
 





 \-     
 
**Standing up and hardening our infrastructure:** 

 Terraform\-managed AWS, deployment pipelines, database strategy, and the security practices that keep sensitive client data safe.
 




  





 Who You Are
 

 \-     
 **A fullstack engineer with 1\-3 years of experience.** 

 You may specialize, but if backend work doesn’t resonate with you or you would rather not touch design on the frontend, this is not the right fit. We want engineers who love the whole stack.
 




 \-     
 **Design\-minded.** 

 You believe it is not enough for software to merely work—it should look, feel, and function beautifully.
 




 \-     
 **Product\-minded.** 

 You never assume you know what users want; translating their needs into the right work is the heart of the job. This is, candidly, the hardest part of engineering. It takes patience, intuition, humility, and the confidence to be comfortable “not knowing” and the skills to "figure it out”.
 




 \-     
 **A strong writer.** 

 Much of our work lives in documentation, RFCs, and clear explanations of what we've built and why.
 




 \-     
 **A continuous learner.** 

 If reading documentation, taking a course, or digging into something unfamiliar sounds like a chore, this is not the place for you.
 




 \-     
 **Energized by AI.** 

 You are eager to work with it, learn to wield it well, and figure out where it belongs in what we build.
 




 \-     
 **Thrives in a culture of accountability and ownership.** 

 We run on a strong culture of accountability and ownership. You must have the confidence to speak candidly, disagree openly, own your work, and a genuine desire to grow.
 




  





 Location
 


 LoVasco is based in Detroit, Michigan, where most of our team works out of our downtown office most days. Engineering works out of a co\-working space in Washington, DC. We're a hybrid team, and we believe that flexibility is supported and sustained by a strong culture of accountability and ownership.
 




  





 Career Path
 


 Engineering exists to help LoVasco grow. As software becomes a larger part of our growth strategy, engineers will take on more complex projects, grow and manage larger teams, and play a bigger role in the company's success. And as the firm wins, we want our engineers to win with it—the firm's success should be the engineer's success, too. Engineers grow by building products that make a real impact on the organization. That's our goal, that's our challenge, and that's what motivates us.
 




  





 Benefits
 


 We invest in our people, and our benefits reflect it:
 




 \-     
 **Health coverage,** 

 through plans we sponsor, that are affordable and have excellent coverage options, including FSA and HSA.
 




 \-     
 **A 401(k) with a 4% matching contribution** 

 , plus access to the same professionals and education resources our participants have—the tools to save, build financial security, and chart your future.
 




 \-     
 **Performance\-based bonus programs** 

 that supplement your compensation and reward both your individual performance and the company's profitability.
 




 \-     
 **Flexible, hybrid work** 

 , with co\-working subscriptions for employees outside the Detroit area.
 





 \-     
 
**Generous Paid Time Off,** 

 starting at 20 days per year, nine holidays, and Summer Fridays.
 




 \-     
 **A learning budget** 

 for resources, continuous learning, and attending live conferences and conventions.
 




 \-     
 **Biannual all\-company meeting weeks** 

 in Detroit.
 





 \-     
 
**Life insurance, short and long term disability insurance,** 

 paid for by the company, including salary continuance.
 




  






 ﻿

 : $85 \- $100k; Competitive base salary, commensurate with experience, plus performance\-based bonuses tied to your impact and the firm's success.

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Conduct deep data analysis to derive insights for the business, identify gaps, and uncover new opportunities.

Job Title: Machine Learning Engineer / Researcher (AI\-Powered CAD, YC Startup)
 



 Job Location: San Mateo, CA
 



 Job Duration: Full\-Time Permanent
 



 Salary: $110,000 \- $175,000/Year
 



  





 Job Overview
 



 In this role, you'll navigate the dynamic intersection of research and engineering as you oversee the entire lifecycle of machine learning systems for an AI\-driven CAD product. Your day\-to\-day will involve diving deep into research and hands\-on engineering tasks, collaborating directly with the founders to define problem scopes and converting raw geometry and design data into valuable training signals. You'll innovate by designing and training custom deep learning models that enhance CAD workflows, predicting optimal next steps. Your expertise will be pivotal in building and maintaining robust Python pipelines for training and evaluating these models. Ensuring the rapid and reliable integration of ML features into CAD environments will be part of your core responsibilities, and you'll architect backend components to support this goal. You'll work closely with mechanical and hardware engineers, translating their workflows into concrete ML formulations. Ownership over the ML features will span from research to productionization, requiring you to lead experiments, model comparisons, and production deployments while ensuring steady improvements through best practices in logging and evaluation. You'll thrive in a fast\-moving startup environment, where you can leverage your deep expertise with modern deep learning frameworks, like PyTorch, and your ability to solve open\-ended problems by devising and implementing novel architecture. This is an opportunity for a foundational role where you'll not only steer ML projects but also influence the future of AI\-powered CAD design. The ideal candidate possesses a robust background in machine learning, significant experience in designing and deploying models, and a passion for pushing the boundaries of engineering innovation.
 



  





 Responsibilities:
 



 As Hestus’s machine learning research engineer, you’ll own the full lifecycle of ML systems that power our AI\-driven CAD product. You’ll move between deep research and hands\-on engineering: scoping problems with the founders, designing and training novel models, and getting them into robust production code. A big part of the role is turning messy, real\-world geometry and design data into usable training signals, then iterating quickly based on performance, reliability, and customer feedback. You’ll collaborate closely with our backend engineers on data pipelines, APIs, and infra, and you’ll play a key role in setting technical direction for how we apply ML to accelerate hardware design.

About Flotive AI
 
  





 A solar farm sits dead for eight months because someone missed a county setback ordinance buried on page 340 of a zoning code. A transmission line gets rerouted, at a cost of millions, because an environmental filing cited the wrong watershed. A data center waits months for power because a utility and developer are working from different versions of the interconnection rules.
 



  





 This isn't an engineering problem or a capital problem. It's an information problem. The rules that decide whether America gets built are scattered across thousands of agencies and millions of pages of regulatory text. Searching, cross\-referencing, and verification has been a manual process, becoming the primary determinants of how long it takes for a project to get built.
 



  





 Flotive fixes that. We build AI systems that continuously ingest regulations, technical standards, permitting requirements, and agency guidance; understand how they relate to specific projects and locations; and produce verifiable, explainable answers backed by primary sources. Our customers spend less time searching for requirements and more time designing, permitting, and building. We’re starting with power projects, but our work has the potential to have far reaching impacts on all types of developments\- from housing to mining.
 



  





 Our mission is simple:
 


**Help society build and run infrastructure while maintaining the highest standards of safety, environmental stewardship, and regulatory compliance.** 

  





 We believe better information and workflows, not weaker regulation, is the fastest path to building the infrastructure society needs. By reducing the time and cost of regulatory compliance, we can accelerate projects while improving transparency, consistency, and trust in the process.
 



  





  




 About the role
 
  





 As a Founding Software Engineer at Flotive, you will work closely with the co\-founders (Francis and Akshay), other engineers, and subject matter experts to understand customer requirements, and own and make decisions on technical architecture before anyone else gets hired to weigh in on them. an always up\-to\-date decision\-making framework that leverages verifiable AI grounded in regulatory documents and other authoritative sources.
 



  





 The technical core of this job is building a system that ingests regulatory documents at scale, extracts structured knowledge from them, tracks geographic and jurisdictional context, and produces workflows that customer can trust and verify. That means real problems in retrieval, processing, knowledge representation, geospatial reasoning, and customer\-facing decision workflows, not CRUD endpoints wrapped around a database.
 



  





 This is a high ownership role on a small but elite team, where your decisions will directly shape the customer experience and the company.

**Description**
 Come keep one of the world's largest Apache Kafka fleets healthy, secure, and always on. On Amazon MSK, you will build the automation that maintains hundreds of thousands of streaming hosts, so customers never have to think about the infrastructure underneath their applications.
   

  

 This is infrastructure engineering at a scale where every change has to be safe by design. MSK is stateful: every host holds customer data that must stay replicated and in sync, so routine maintenance is never as simple as rebooting or replacing a host. Patching, repairing, and replacing nodes across a fleet this size means coordinating each action against the availability guarantees customers depend on, so that maintenance stays invisible to them.
   

  

 You will design and build the automation that does this, turning hard operational problems into systems that run themselves. If you enjoy distributed systems, large\-scale automation, and work whose reliability countless streaming applications quietly depend on, this is a rare place to do it.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design, build, and operate automation that patches and maintains hundreds of thousands of stateful hosts, keeping fleet maintenance invisible to customers.
* Build systems that automatically detect unhealthy hosts and remediate them, balancing fast recovery against avoiding needless disruption.
* Develop rollout and rollback mechanisms that keep the blast radius of any change small at fleet scale, and that let changes be tested before they reach customers and reversed if something goes wrong.
* Own your services end to end: take part in on\-call, debug production issues, and continually reduce the manual effort needed to operate the fleet.
* Write design documents, collaborate with engineers across MSK, and raise the engineering bar through design and code reviews.


 A day in the life
   

  

 No two days look the same, but most blend building with operating. You might spend the morning designing a safer way to roll out a fleet\-wide change, pairing with a teammate on the review, and writing the automation that carries it out. In the afternoon you might dig into a signal that a small set of hosts is unhealthy, trace it to root cause, and improve the automation so it handles that case on its own next time. You will write design documents, review your teammates' code, and steadily push routine operational work out of human hands and into systems that run themselves. When you are on call, you keep the fleet healthy and feed every manual step you take back into automation, so the same issue does not page anyone twice.
   

  

 Our team keeps Amazon MSK's managed Kafka fleet healthy, secure, and available, so customers never have to think about the infrastructure beneath their streaming applications. People choose MSK because they want Apache Kafka without the burden of operating it. Our mission is to make that promise real at very large scale: keeping the fleet patched and secure, automatically recovering hosts that become unhealthy, and renewing the certificates that protect data in transit, all without interrupting the applications running on top.
   

  

 We believe operations should be automated, not heroic. We invest in systems that detect and resolve problems on their own, so the team spends its time building durable automation instead of reacting to pages, and we are increasingly using generative AI to strengthen those mechanisms. You will build alongside teammates who jointly own these systems, and you will partner with the wider MSK engineering, product, and operations groups that depend on the fleet staying healthy as the service grows. Your work shapes the reliability every MSK customer feels, and you will have real ownership of meaningful problems from design through operation.

**Description**
 Come keep one of the world's largest Apache Kafka fleets healthy, secure, and always on. On Amazon MSK, you will build the automation that maintains hundreds of thousands of streaming hosts, so customers never have to think about the infrastructure underneath their applications.
   

  

 This is infrastructure engineering at a scale where every change has to be safe by design. MSK is stateful: every host holds customer data that must stay replicated and in sync, so routine maintenance is never as simple as rebooting or replacing a host. Patching, repairing, and replacing nodes across a fleet this size means coordinating each action against the availability guarantees customers depend on, so that maintenance stays invisible to them.
   

  

 You will design and build the automation that does this, turning hard operational problems into systems that run themselves. If you enjoy distributed systems, large\-scale automation, and work whose reliability countless streaming applications quietly depend on, this is a rare place to do it.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design, build, and operate automation that patches and maintains hundreds of thousands of stateful hosts, keeping fleet maintenance invisible to customers.
* Build systems that automatically detect unhealthy hosts and remediate them, balancing fast recovery against avoiding needless disruption.
* Develop rollout and rollback mechanisms that keep the blast radius of any change small at fleet scale, and that let changes be tested before they reach customers and reversed if something goes wrong.
* Own your services end to end: take part in on\-call, debug production issues, and continually reduce the manual effort needed to operate the fleet.
* Write design documents, collaborate with engineers across MSK, and raise the engineering bar through design and code reviews.


 A day in the life
   

  

 No two days look the same, but most blend building with operating. You might spend the morning designing a safer way to roll out a fleet\-wide change, pairing with a teammate on the review, and writing the automation that carries it out. In the afternoon you might dig into a signal that a small set of hosts is unhealthy, trace it to root cause, and improve the automation so it handles that case on its own next time. You will write design documents, review your teammates' code, and steadily push routine operational work out of human hands and into systems that run themselves. When you are on call, you keep the fleet healthy and feed every manual step you take back into automation, so the same issue does not page anyone twice.
   

  

 Our team keeps Amazon MSK's managed Kafka fleet healthy, secure, and available, so customers never have to think about the infrastructure beneath their streaming applications. People choose MSK because they want Apache Kafka without the burden of operating it. Our mission is to make that promise real at very large scale: keeping the fleet patched and secure, automatically recovering hosts that become unhealthy, and renewing the certificates that protect data in transit, all without interrupting the applications running on top.
   

  

 We believe operations should be automated, not heroic. We invest in systems that detect and resolve problems on their own, so the team spends its time building durable automation instead of reacting to pages, and we are increasingly using generative AI to strengthen those mechanisms. You will build alongside teammates who jointly own these systems, and you will partner with the wider MSK engineering, product, and operations groups that depend on the fleet staying healthy as the service grows. Your work shapes the reliability every MSK customer feels, and you will have real ownership of meaningful problems from design through operation.

 At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.
   

  

 Our Science \& Technology directorates include National Security, Earth and Biological Sciences, Physical and Computational Sciences, and Energy and Environment.  in ACMDD at PNNL seeks a Data Scientist to join the group to lead and support scientific research in robotics, autonomous systems, and intelligent control.  You will work closely with AI product teams, clinical and technical stakeholders, DevOps engineers, and the AI Governance Committee to engineer scalable data flows that support model validation, real\-time monitoring, and Machine Learning Engineer I will be primarily responsible for contributing to the development and enhancement of machine learning applications and systems. **About the Team**
 The HIL Platform and Services team in GM’s Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Organization is responsible for developing and scaling high\-fidelity, reliable Hardware\-in\-the\-Loop (HIL) validation platforms that test AV software before it’s deployed to vehicles.  We build and operate the systems that let AV teams validate perception, planning, control, and AI models against real hardware interfaces and complex scenarios, long before they reach the road.

 As a Software Engineer on the HIL Platform and Services team, you will be at the intersection of AV software and AI models and the hardware systems that enable vehicle autonomy. You will work closely with teams across the AV organization – including Embodied AI, Model Deployment, Middleware, OS, Sensor Applications, and Vehicle Integration – to build the software and tooling that make large\-scale HIL validation possible.
   

  

 This is an early\-career / new graduate role designed for candidates who have recently or will be completing their degree by June 2026\. You will be paired with experienced engineers to help you ramp up on AV Software, the Software HIL platform and services concepts, and our internal HIL platforms themselves.
   

  

**What You’ll Be Doing (Responsibilities)**
* Develop software to increase the capabilities, fidelity, observability, and scale of our HIL platform and integration services.
* Build and extend services and tools that make it easy for AV teams to configure, run, and debug tests on HIL benches.
* Deliver reliable software through clear requirements generation, continuous integration, automated testing, issue tracking, and code reviews.
* Collaborate with colleagues across multiple AV teams to understand their validation needs and translate them into platform features.
* Deliver complex projects through incremental development, iterating quickly while maintaining quality and reliability.
